messages:
maria_p: Quick sync — we need to lock the perf prioritization for next sprint. top candidates: 1) latency SLO work (p99 tail), 2) batching/throughput for peak cost, 3) KV-prefetch + cache warming. also two paid customer asks (Acme wants <200ms, FinCorp cares about cost).
alex_k: +1 to prioritizing latency for the interactive flows. Acme is already pushing.
sophia_m: Agree on latency for chat UI, but quantization/better kernels could hit cost wins across thousands of requests. that's more medium-term though.
jasper_r: Ops note: batching increases complexity of autoscaler and alerting. we need guardrails before shipping.
chris_c: From CS: Acme said they'd sign if we can promise tail latency improvements and a canary rollout window. FinCorp wants 20% unit cost reduction. both are pay customers.
maria_p: Proposal: use a RICE-ish check to pick top 2 workstreams. quick scoring in thread, then we run two 2-week spikes (one latency-focused, one batching/cache-focused) and a lightweight eval harness for regressions.
alex_k: I sketched quick scores, feel free to edit: 
```
Workstream | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort (wks) | RICE-ish score
Latency SLO | 0.35 | 9 | 0.7 | 4 | 0.35*9*0.7/4 = 0.551
Batching/Throughput | 0.5 | 6 | 0.6 | 3 | 0.5*6*0.6/3 = 0.6
KV-prefetch+cache | 0.3 | 5 | 0.5 | 2 | 0.3*5*0.5/2 = 0.375
Quantization pilot | 0.4 | 4 | 0.5 | 3 | 0.4*4*0.5/3 = 0.267
```
alex_k: my read: batching edges out latency by raw RICE score, but latency has higher commercial urgency (Acme).
sophia_m: Important: RICE numbers shouldn't ignore quality/regression risk. quant+kernel changes can reduce cost but add model hallucination risk. put a QA/regression multiplier or separate 'quality debt' flag.
jasper_r: Also add ops effort: batching will require autoscaler policy changes, new metrics, and a fallback path. that's nontrivial and should increase the effort estimate.
maria_p: Good call. let's adjust effort for batching to 5 weeks if we include autoscaler + rollout scripts. that drops the score.
chris_c: For prioritization, commercial weight: if Acme signs, latency gets +0.2 reach impact in our model. FinCorp's cost ask maps to batching/quantization revenue but later.
maria_p: Updated plan: 1) Run a 2-week latency spike focused on tail fixes + a canary plan tied to Acme, goal: p99 drop <200ms for their workload OR clear blocker list. 2) Parallel 2-week feasibility spike for batching + autoscaler changes (POC only). after spikes, we re-run RICE with measured confidence/effort.
alex_k: timeline looks fine. can the latency spike include a light regression harness (10 prompts, eval metrics) so we catch quality regressions?
sophia_m: i'll own a tiny eval harness and add an automated regression check (WER/rouge-like + a few red-team prompts).
jasper_r: i'll prepare an ops checklist for safe rollout: feature flag, canary region, auto-fallback to lower batching, runbook.
maria_p: Next steps: alex + sophia + jasper run spikes starting Mon, ship minimal artifacts by end of sprint. chris to line up Acme test traffic for canary. I'll update the roadmap and prep a one-pager for sales.
chris_c: i'll ping Acme and ask for a short traffic window next week.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: perf-spike-latency -> staging at 1966667799 :rocket:
maria_p: thumbs up. quick vote: thumbs up if you support this plan, :eyes: if you want changes.
alex_k: :+1:
sophia_m: :+1:
jasper_r: :eyes: (verify effort on batching)
chris_c: :+1:
maria_p: awesome. i'll write the acceptance criteria: 
- Latency spike: measurable p99 improvement on Acme test workload OR a clear rollback and list of blockers.
- Batching spike: functional POC that demonstrates 20-40% token-cost reduction on synthetic peak traffic, with notes on autoscaler / fallback.
- Both spikes produce a revised RICE table with measured reach/impact/confidence/effort.
maria_p: tagging this for the roadmap doc, will file followup ticket and share results in next T+1 meeting. Thanks all.
